f.title: Inspections of MAHs and subcontracted third parties by empowered NCA inspectors
f.statement: Competent authorities of the Member States concerned shall conduct, in cooperation with the Agency, pharmacovigilance inspections of marketing authorisation holders or third parties subcontracted for pharmacovigilance tasks (including third parties subcontracted directly by the marketing authorisation holder and those further subcontracted). Inspections shall be carried out by inspectors appointed by the national competent authorities and empowered to inspect the premises, records, documents and PSMF of the marketing authorisation holder or of any third party subcontracted by it or by a subcontracted third party to perform Title IX activities.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Partner & vendor oversight

rows.actor: National competent authorities (in cooperation with the Agency); marketing authorisation holders and subcontracted third parties are inspected
rows.quote: competent authorities of the Member States concerned shall conduct, in cooperation with the Agency, pharmacovigilance inspections of marketing authorisation holders or third parties subcontracted for pharmacovigilance tasks (which includes third parties subcontracted directly by the marketing authorisation holder and third parties further subcontracted by such subcontracted third parties [IR Art 6(3)]) [IR Art 13(1a)]. Such inspections shall be carried out by inspectors appointed by the national competent authorities and empowered to inspect the premises, records, documents and pharmacovigilance system master file (PSMF) of the marketing authorisation holder or any third parties subcontracted by the marketing authorisation holder or by a subcontracted third party to perform the activities described in Title IX of Directive 2001/83/EC in accordance with Articles 111(1), 111(1d) and 111(1g).
rows.review_note: Review: added - missed 'shall' provision defining who is inspected (MAH and all subcontracting tiers) and inspector powers; tracking item for MAH readiness. Double-check: Authority-only duty (NCAs shall inspect, inspectors empowered); quote proves it but kept as tracking row for MAHs and subcontractors, so below 90.

f.title: Provide the PSMF on request for inspection planning and conduct
f.statement: Marketing authorisation holders are required to provide, on request, the pharmacovigilance system master file (PSMF), which will be used for planning and conducting inspections.
f.processes: PSMF management; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder
rows.quote: In particular, marketing authorisation holders are required to provide, on request, the PSMF, which will be used to for planning and conducting inspections [DIR Art 23(4), REG Article 16(3a)] (see GVP Module II).
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote proves the MAH duty ("are required to provide, on request, the PSMF") with legal citation; no change.

f.title: Include the third party's agreement to be inspected in pharmacovigilance subcontracts
f.statement: A third party subcontracted for pharmacovigilance tasks has the obligation to agree in the subcontract to be inspected by competent authorities. This applies mutatis mutandis to third parties that subcontract the tasks subcontracted to them by the marketing authorisation holder.
f.applicability: Subcontracts for pharmacovigilance tasks, including sub-subcontracts
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: Subcontracted third party (and, mutatis mutandis, third parties that further subcontract tasks subcontracted to them by the MAH)
rows.quote: The third party has the obligation to agree to be inspected by competent authorities in the subcontract [IR Art 6(3)]. This applied mutatis mutandis to the third parties that subcontract the tasks subcontracted to them by the marketing authorisation holder [IR Art 6(3)].
rows.review_note: Review: actor clarified: IR Art 6(3)(d) as amended by IR 2025/1466 puts the inclusion of this clause on the MAH (and mutatis mutandis on subcontracting third parties). Level Mandatory kept. Double-check: Quote proves the third party's obligation to agree in the subcontract to be inspected. Actor simplified to the quoted actor; the reviewer's reference to IR 2025/1466 is not in this text and was not relied on. RACI maps the duty to the MAH's contract owner (inferred), so below 90.

f.title: Document inspection arrangements where a subcontractor further subcontracts tasks
f.statement: Where a subcontracted third party subcontracts one or more pharmacovigilance tasks to another third party, inspection arrangements should be clearly documented.
f.applicability: Pharmacovigilance tasks further subcontracted by a subcontracted third party
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: Subcontracted third party that further subcontracts tasks (and the marketing authorisation holder; inferred, the source uses passive wording)
rows.quote: Also, where a subcontracted third party subcontracts (a) task(s) to another third party, inspections arrangements should be clearly documented [IR Art 6(3)].
rows.review_note: Review: flag decided: Mandatory kept. GVP uses 'should', but the cited IR Art 6(3)(c) (IR 2025/1466) requires subcontracts to include 'arrangements for inspection and auditing process of third parties', applied mutatis mutandis to sub-subcontracting; statement now states this legal basis. Actor widened to the MAH overseeing. Double-check: Statement trimmed to what the quote says; the reviewer's reliance on IR Art 6(3)(c) / IR 2025/1466 is not in this text and was removed. Level changed Mandatory -> Recommended: the quote uses "should" (the module uses "should" for guidance). Passive wording, so who documents the arrangements is inferred (subcontracting third party / MAH); judgement-call level and inferred actor, so below 90.

f.title: Locate the PSMF at the EU main PV site or the EU QPPV site
f.statement: The PSMF shall be located either at the site in the EU where the main pharmacovigilance activities of the marketing authorisation holder are performed or at the site in the EU where the QPPV operates.
f.processes: PSMF management; Safety governance

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder
rows.quote: The PSMF shall be located either at the site in the EU where the main pharmacovigilance activities of the marketing authorisation holder are performed or at the site in the EU where the qualified person responsible for Guideline on good pharmacovigilance practices (GVP) – Module III (Rev 2) EMA/119871/2012 Rev 2 of 4 September 2026 Page 3/19 pharmacovigilance in the EU (QPPV) operates [IR Art 7(1)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote proves the Mandatory PSMF location duty, but it contains page-header text across the page break and the actor (MAH) is implied by passive wording, so below 90.

f.title: Supervisory authority for CAPs is the NCA of the Member State where the PSMF is located
f.statement: The supervisory authority for pharmacovigilance shall be the competent authority of the Member State in which the PSMF is located.
f.applicability: Centrally authorised products (context given by the preceding sentence of III.A)
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; PSMF management

rows.actor: Competent authority of the Member State where the PSMF is located (supervisory authority); relevant to marketing authorisation holders
rows.quote: The supervisory authority for pharmacovigilance shall be the competent authority of the Member State in which the PSMF is located [REG Art 18(3)].
rows.review_note: Review: added - missed 'shall' provision; the MAH's PSMF location determines its supervisory authority (repeated in III.C.4.2). Double-check: Statement trimmed to the quote: the CAP context and the verification role come from the preceding sentence (REG Art 19), not the quote; REG Art 19 removed from legal_basis. Authority-designation row, so below 90.

f.title: Expect possible pre-authorisation inspections by the supervisory authority
f.statement: The supervisory authority may conduct pre-authorisation inspections to verify the accuracy and successful implementation of the existing or proposed pharmacovigilance system.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: Supervisory authority for pharmacovigilance
rows.quote: The supervisory authority may conduct pre-authorisation inspections to verify the accuracy and successful implementation of the existing or proposed pharmacovigilance system [REG Art 19(1)].
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority row kept as tracking item for applicants (CAP pre-authorisation inspection possibility). Double-check: Permitted authority power, quoted exactly; authority-only tracking row, so below 90.

f.title: Provide inspection results to the inspected entity with an opportunity to comment
f.statement: The results of an inspection shall be provided to the inspected entity, who shall be given the opportunity to comment.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Competent authority of the Member State (inspected entity comments)
rows.quote: The results of an inspection shall be provided to the inspected entity, who shall be given the opportunity to comment [DIR Art 111(3) and (8)].
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Mandatory authority duty quoted exactly with legal citation; authority-only row (MAH only comments), so below 90.

f.title: Rectify inspection non-compliance in a timely manner through a CAPA plan
f.statement: Any non-compliance should be rectified by the marketing authorisation holder in a timely manner through the implementation of a corrective and preventive action plan.
f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder
rows.quote: Any non-compliance should also be rectified by the marketing authorisation holder in a timely manner through the implementation of a corrective and preventive action plan.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Quote proves "should" duty on the MAH to rectify non-compliance through a CAPA plan; level, actor and statement match.

f.title: For-cause inspections may follow recognised triggers
f.statement: For-cause pharmacovigilance inspections are undertaken when a trigger is recognised and an inspection is considered an appropriate way to examine the issues. They are more likely to focus on specific pharmacovigilance processes or on identified compliance issues and their impact for a specific medicinal product, but full system inspections may also result from a trigger. For-cause inspections may arise when, for example, one or more of the triggers listed in III.B.1.2 are identified.
f.clause: III.B.1.2. Routine and for-cause pharmacovigilance inspections
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: National competent authority (inspectorate); marketing authorisation holder is inspected
rows.quote: For-cause pharmacovigilance inspections are undertaken when a trigger is recognised, and an inspection is considered an appropriate way to examine the issues. For-cause inspections are more likely to focus on specific pharmacovigilance processes or to include an examination of identified compliance issues and their impact for a specific medicinal product. However, full pharmacovigilance system inspections may also be performed resulting from a trigger. For-cause inspections may arise when, for example, one or more of the triggers listed below are identified:
rows.location: III.B.1.2. Routine and for-cause pharmacovigilance inspections
rows.review_note: Review: added as tracking item - triggers (late/poor reporting, unmet RMP commitments, CAPA delays, public communication without prior notice, etc.) indicate what exposes an MAH to for-cause inspection. Double-check: Descriptive wording ("are undertaken", "may arise"); Permitted level is a judgement call, authority-only tracking row, and the trigger list is not quoted, so well below 90.

f.title: Possible outcomes of a pre-authorisation inspection that raises concerns
f.statement: If the outcome of the pre-authorisation inspection raises concerns about the applicant's ability to comply with the requirements of the Regulation and the Directive, the recommendations that may be considered include not granting the marketing authorisation, or re-inspection prior to marketing authorisation to confirm that critical findings and recommendations have been addressed.
f.applicability: Applicants subject to a pre-authorisation inspection
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Competent authorities / CHMP
rows.quote: If the outcome of the pre-authorisation inspection raises concerns about the applicant’s ability to comply with the requirements laid down in the Regulation and the Directive, the following recommendations may be considered: • Not granting the marketing authorisation; • Re-inspection prior to marketing authorisation to confirm that critical findings and recommendations have been addressed;
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted tracking row kept; the third option (grant with recommendation for an early post-authorisation inspection) added as new row EMA-GVP-III-R2-0037 because the quote cannot run across 'post-/authorisation' (line-end hyphen). Double-check: Permitted options ("may be considered") quoted with bullets; authority/CHMP-only tracking row, so below 90.

f.title: Pre-authorisation inspection findings influence the timing of a routine programme inspection
f.statement: In this case, the findings of the pre-authorisation inspection would influence the timing of an inspection conducted as part of the EU routine programme of pharmacovigilance inspections (see III.B.2).
f.applicability: Applicants subject to a pre-authorisation inspection
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: Competent authorities / CHMP (inferred; the quote names no actor)
rows.quote: In this case, the findings would influence the timing of an inspection conducted as part of the EU routine programme of pharmacovigilance inspections (see III.B.2.);
rows.review_note: Review: added - option dropped by the extractor; the preceding words ('Granting the marketing authorisation with the recommendation to perform an early post-authorisation pharmacovigilance inspection') cannot be quoted because 'post-/authorisation' is split at a line-end hyphen, so the quote is the following sentence of the same bullet and the statement names the option from the bullet's start. Double-check: Quote does not contain the option itself (granting the MA with a recommended early post-authorisation inspection) because that bullet breaks at the line-end hyphen "post-/authorisation" and cannot be quoted. Statement and title reduced to what the quote proves (findings influence timing of a routine programme inspection); "In this case" refers to that option in III.B.1.3, third bullet. Descriptive "would", level Permitted is a judgement call; authority-only. Needs admin review.

f.title: Safety conditions may be imposed on the marketing authorisation after a pre-authorisation inspection
f.statement: Following a pre-authorisation inspection that raises concerns, imposition of safety conditions on the marketing authorisation may be considered.
f.applicability: Applicants subject to a pre-authorisation inspection
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Risk management & minimisation

rows.actor: Competent authorities / CHMP
rows.quote: Imposition of safety conditions to the marketing authorisation [based on DIR Art 21a and REG Art 9(4)].
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Double-check: Quote is a bullet without its lead-in ("the following recommendations may be considered"); the Permitted level and the pre-authorisation context come from the lead-in, and the row is authority-only, so below 90.

f.title: Be aware inspections may be unannounced or announced at short notice
f.statement: Most inspections are anticipated to be announced, i.e. notified in advance to the inspected party, to ensure availability of relevant individuals. On occasion it may be appropriate to conduct unannounced inspections or to announce an inspection at short notice, for example when announcement could compromise the inspection objectives or when the inspection is conducted in a short timeframe for urgent safety reasons.
f.exceptions: Unannounced or short-notice inspections where announcement could compromise objectives or for urgent safety reasons
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: National competent authority (inspectorate)
rows.quote: It is anticipated that the majority of inspections will be announced, i.e. notified in advance to the inspected party, to ensure the availability of relevant individuals for the inspection. However, on occasion, it may be appropriate to conduct unannounced inspections or to announce an inspection at short notice (e.g. when the announcement could compromise the objectives of the inspection or when the inspection is conducted in a short timeframe due to urgent safety reasons).
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Double-check: Permitted authority option quoted exactly; deadline field cleared (advance notification is not a time frame). Authority-only tracking row, so below 90.

f.title: Early re-inspection where significant non-compliance or failed CAPA implementation
f.statement: Early re-inspection may take place where significant non-compliance has been identified and it is necessary to verify actions taken to address findings and evaluate ongoing compliance, including changes in the pharmacovigilance system. Early re-inspection may also be appropriate when a previous inspection showed the inspected party had failed to implement corrective and preventive actions appropriately in response to an earlier inspection.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: National competent authority (inspectorate)
rows.quote: Early re-inspection may take place where significant non-compliance has been identified and where it is necessary to verify actions taken to address findings and to evaluate ongoing compliance with the obligations, including evaluation of changes in the pharmacovigilance system. Early re-inspection may also be appropriate when it is known from a previous inspection that the inspected party had failed to implement appropriately corrective and preventive actions in response to an earlier inspection.
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Double-check: Permitted authority option quoted exactly; authority-only tracking row, so below 90.

f.title: Decide on remote inspection considering feasibility of remote interviews and document access
f.statement: The inspectorate may decide case by case whether a remote inspection will be sufficient to gain an adequate overview of the marketing authorisation holder's pharmacovigilance system. The decision should consider whether it is feasible to arrange interviews of relevant staff and review of documentation, including the safety database, source documents and PSMF, via remote access.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: National competent authority (inspectorate)
rows.quote: The inspectorate may decide on a case-by-case basis whether a remote inspection will be sufficient to gain an adequate overview of the functioning of the marketing authorisation holder’s pharmacovigilance system. This decision should take into in consideration whether it is feasible to arrange interviews of relevant staff and review of documentation, including the safety database, source documents and PSMF, via remote access.
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Double-check: Quote proves "may decide" and "should take into consideration"; mixed level (Permitted kept as the main verb) and authority-only row, so below 90.

f.title: Use IT solutions to give inspectors remote access and support
f.statement: Different information technology (IT) solutions may be used to provide access to electronic systems and maintain communication with and support to inspectors during remote inspections.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Safety system configuration

rows.actor: Marketing authorisation holder / subcontracted third parties
rows.quote: Different information technology (IT) solutions may be used to provide access to electronic systems and maintain communication with and support to inspectors.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: Permitted, passive wording: who uses the IT solutions (MAH / subcontracted third parties) is inferred from the remote inspections context, so below 90.

f.title: Respond to authority requests for information for risk-based inspection planning
f.statement: National competent authorities and the Agency may solicit information from marketing authorisation holders for risk-based inspection planning purposes if it is not readily available elsewhere.
f.exceptions: Only if the information is not readily available elsewhere
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Submission operations

rows.actor: National competent authorities and the Agency (marketing authorisation holder responds)
rows.quote: National competent authorities and the Agency may solicit information from marketing authorisation holders for risk-based inspection planning purposes if it is not readily available elsewhere.
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Double-check: Permitted authority power quoted exactly; authority-only tracking row (MAH response implied), so below 90.

f.title: Sites outside the EU may be inspected
f.statement: Sites to be inspected may be located in the EU (e.g. PSMF location or EU QPPV site) or outside the EU. Inspections of sites outside the EU might be appropriate where the main pharmacovigilance centre, databases and/or activities are outside the EU and it would otherwise be inefficient or impossible to confirm compliance from an EU site.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: National competent authority (inspectorate)
rows.quote: The sites to be inspected may be located in the EU (e.g. PSMF location or EU QPPV site) or outside the EU. Inspections of sites outside the EU might be appropriate where the main pharmacovigilance centre, databases and/or activities are located outside the EU and it would be otherwise inefficient or impossible to confirm compliance from a site within the EU.
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Double-check: Permitted/descriptive ("may be located", "might be appropriate"); authority-only tracking row, so below 90.

f.title: Subcontracted third parties may be inspected even without an inspection clause
f.statement: Any third party subcontracted to conduct pharmacovigilance tasks in whole or in part on behalf of or with the marketing authorisation holder may be inspected to confirm its capability to support the marketing authorisation holder's compliance, even if the third party's obligation to agree to be inspected has not yet been included in the subcontract.
f.processes: Partner & vendor oversight; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: Competent authorities (subcontracted third parties are subject)
rows.quote: Any third party subcontracted to conduct pharmacovigilance tasks in whole or in part on behalf of or in conjunction with the marketing authorisation holder may be inspected, in order to confirm their capability to support the marketing authorisation holder’s compliance with pharmacovigilance obligations, even if the obligation of the third parties to agree to be inspected by competent authorities has not yet been included in the subcontract [IR Art 13(1a)].
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Double-check: Permitted authority power quoted exactly with legal citation; authority-only tracking row, so below 90.

f.title: Additional data may be requested in advance of an inspection
f.statement: It may be appropriate for additional data to be requested in advance of an inspection, in order to select appropriate sites or clarify aspects of the pharmacovigilance system.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: National competent authority (inspectorate)
rows.quote: It may be appropriate for additional data to be requested in advance of an inspection, in order to select appropriate sites or clarify aspects of the pharmacovigilance system.
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Double-check: Passive wording ("may be appropriate for additional data to be requested"): requester (inspectorate) and responder are inferred; authority-only, so below 90.

f.title: Inspection follow-up continues until the CAPA plan is completed
f.statement: When non-compliance with pharmacovigilance obligations is identified during an inspection, follow-up will be required until a corrective and preventive action plan is completed. Follow-up actions to be considered include review of the marketing authorisation holder's corrective and preventive action plan, review of periodic progress reports when deemed necessary, and re-inspection to assess appropriate implementation of the plan.
f.processes: Quality system & CAPA; Audit & inspection readiness

rows.actor: National competent authority (inspectorate); marketing authorisation holder subject to follow-up
rows.deadline: Until the corrective and preventive action plan is completed
rows.quote: When non-compliance with pharmacovigilance obligations is identified during an inspection, follow-up will be required until a corrective and preventive action plan is completed. The following follow-up actions should be considered, as appropriate: • Review of the marketing authorisation holder’s corrective and preventive action plan; • Review of the periodic progress reports, when deemed necessary; • Re-inspection to assess appropriate implementation of the corrective and preventive action plan;
rows.review_note: Review: flag decided: level Mandatory -> Recommended. 'Follow-up will be required' is the guideline's own expectation with no legal citation (the module marks legal requirements with 'shall' and a reference), and the listed actions are 'should be considered'. Actor names the MAH as the party followed up. Double-check: Level change Mandatory -> Recommended reviewed and kept as a judgement call: "follow-up will be required" has no legal citation and the listed actions "should be considered". The follow-up is an authority activity; the MAH is the party followed up. Judgement-call level and authority-only row, so below 90.

f.title: Possible follow-up requests: data, variations, impact analyses, communications, meetings
f.statement: Follow-up actions should be considered as appropriate, including requests for submission of previously un-submitted data, submission of variations (e.g. to amend product information), submission of impact analyses (e.g. following review of data not previously considered in routine signal detection), requests for issuing safety communications including amendments of marketing and/or advertising information, and requests for a meeting with the marketing authorisation holder to discuss the deficiencies, their impact and action plans.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Submission operations; Safety communications

rows.actor: National competent authority (marketing authorisation holder responds)
rows.quote: Requests for submission of previously un-submitted data; submission of variations, e.g. to amend product information; submission of impact analyses, e.g. following review of data that were not previously considered during routine signal detection activities; • Requests for issuing safety communications, including amendments of marketing and/or advertising information; • Requests for a meeting with the marketing authorisation holder to discuss the deficiencies, the impact of the deficiencies and action plans;
rows.review_note: Review: no change; Recommended matches 'should be considered'. Authority-only row, so below 90.

f.title: Non-compliant MAHs may face national penalties and Commission financial penalties
f.statement: Where appropriate, the Member State concerned shall take the necessary measures to ensure that a marketing authorisation holder is subject to effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties. The European Commission is empowered to impose financial penalties on holders of marketing authorisations granted under Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 to enforce certain obligations connected with those authorisations.
f.exceptions: Commission financial penalties apply to centrally authorised products (Regulation (EC) No 726/2004)
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Safety governance

rows.actor: Member State concerned; European Commission (marketing authorisation holder is subject to penalties)
rows.quote: Where appropriate, the Member State concerned shall take the necessary measures to ensure that a marketing authorisation holder is subject to effective, proportionate and dissuasive penalties [DIR Art 111(8)]. Moreover, the European Commission is empowered to impose financial penalties on the holders of marketing authorisations to ensure the enforcement of certain obligations connected with marketing authorisations for medicinal products granted in accordance with Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 [REG Art 84a].
rows.review_note: Review: added - skipped penalty provisions state an MAH-relevant consequence (MAH subject to penalties, DIR Art 111(8); Commission financial penalties, REG Art 84a). Also stated in III.A; quoted once from III.B.7. Double-check: Mandatory duty of the Member State and empowerment of the Commission quoted with citations; authority-only row (MAH is subject to penalties), so below 90.

f.title: Regulator meetings to review the MAH's CAPA proposals
f.statement: As a regulatory option (education and facilitation), national competent authorities may communicate with marketing authorisation holder representatives to clarify the legal requirements and the regulator's expectations and to review the marketing authorisation holder's proposals for corrective and preventive actions.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.actor: National competent authority
rows.quote: to clarify the legal requirements and the expectations of the regulator, and to review the marketing authorisation holder’s proposals for corrective and preventive actions;
rows.review_note: Review: Permitted authority/inspectorate row kept as tracking item (sets what the MAH may face); no other change. Actor and Permitted level come from the lead-in; authority-only, so below 90.

f.title: Act on warning letters, non-compliance statements or infringement notices within the stated timeframe
f.statement: Competent authorities may issue warning letters, non-compliance statements or infringement notices (non-statutory or statutory instruments under national legislation) stating the legislation and guideline breached, reminding marketing authorisation holders of their obligations, or specifying the steps that the marketing authorisation holder must take and in what timeframe.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.deadline: Timeframe specified by the competent authority in the instrument

f.title: Seriously or persistently non-compliant MAHs may be publicly listed
f.statement: Among the possible regulatory options in the event of non-compliance, competent authorities may consider making public a list of marketing authorisation holders found to be seriously or persistently non-compliant.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Safety governance

rows.actor: Competent authorities (marketing authorisation holder may be listed)
rows.quote: Competent authorities may consider making public a list of marketing authorisation holders found to be seriously or persistently non-compliant;

f.title: Possible actions against authorisations and other sanctions for PV non-compliance
f.statement: In the event of non-compliance, possible regulatory options include actions against a marketing authorisation or application (urgent safety restriction; variation; suspension or revocation; delays in granting new authorisations until corrective and preventive actions have been implemented, or addition of safety conditions to new authorisations; requests for pre-authorisation inspections), product recalls, action on marketing or advertising information, amendment or suspension of clinical trials for product-specific safety issues, administrative penalties, and referral for criminal prosecution with possible imprisonment under national legislation.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Safety governance

rows.actor: Competent authorities, the Agency or the European Commission (marketing authorisation holder is subject)
rows.quote: Urgent safety restriction; − Variation of the marketing authorisation; − Suspension or revocation of the marketing authorisation; − Delays in granting of new marketing authorisation applications until corrective and preventive actions have been implemented or the addition of safety conditions to new authorisations; − Requests for pre-authorisation inspections; • Product recalls, e.g. where important safety warnings have been omitted from product information; • Action relating to marketing or advertising information; • Amendments or suspension of clinical trials due to medicinal product-specific safety issues; • Administrative penalties, usually fixed fines or based on company profits or levied on a daily basis; • Referral for criminal prosecution with the possibility of imprisonment in accordance with national legislation.
